corrections.subject: validation without overlap with the development samples

result.definition: Validation sample of rule 1.0.7 (56 observations, 34 sampled corrections) without overlap with the development samples: (a) observation level - drop the 6 named cases (inspected before rule 1.0.0 and present in every sample) and every accession that is also in sec-sample-development.json or sec-sample-development-2.json; (b) issuer level (stricter) - additionally drop every issuer (securityId) that appears in a development sample. Unconfirmed counts as not confirmed.
result.reading: Only the observation-level fresh subset is an out-of-sample check of rule 1.0.7; for 1.0.8 (decided after this sample, exclusions only) the still-corrected share is in-sample. 18 of 19 fresh corrections that 1.0.8 keeps are confirmed (the 19th is unconfirmed, none wrong); the Wilson lower bound is the honest summary, not the point share.

corrections.subject: wrong statement in rule-1.0.8.json (amendments[1.0.8].validation)
corrections.wrong: For 1.0.8 the sampled corrections that remain are 32/32 confirmed
corrections.correct: Of the 34 corrections sampled from register 1.0.7, 30 remain corrected under 1.0.8: 29 confirmed, 1 unconfirmed (LOCO 10-Q 2022), 0 wrong (sec-adjudication-validation.json summary.underRule1_0_8); in-sample. The rule file is frozen (sha256 sidecar) and is not edited; this note supersedes the sentence.

corrections.subject: label rowsValueScoreChanged in impact-1.0.0.json
corrections.correct: The counter counts every row whose value score differs by any amount. The value score is a cross-sectional percentile (scale in valueScoreBreakdown.scoreScale): removing or correcting a few market caps shifts the ranks of all rows of the date, so every row with a value score differs (identical to availability.value.before). It is not the number of rows changed by the correction; see valueScoreBreakdown.
